reason: Keep validation, recovery and test ownership minimal and evidence-driven.
Map core/proto/platform/daemon/CLI contracts and keep one decoder per boundary.
Preserve macOS/Linux behavior and Windows checkout/compile contracts.
Reuse the existing effective-account, terminal and infrastructure boundaries.
Refactor account lookup without changing the proven PTY ownership/lifecycle contract.
Keep daemon composition and revision ownership compatible with the retained driver.
Retain official N0 as product default and self-hosted Relay as an explicit separate profile.
Preserve the approved local selector and one-SessionService self-attach boundary.
Preserve the approved per-user detached daemon and no-autostart decision.
Preserve setup-time identity generation and uninstall/reinstall identity semantics.
Use the proven macOS/Linux/Windows compilation and PTY platform boundary.
Avoid holding shared process locks across waits and avoid retry-masking concurrency defects.
Start from the actual Foundation code and avoid recreating or skipping retained layers.
Use the selected Rust 1.98, SQLite, file-lock, peer-credential and detach primitives.
